# Psalm 49 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. A psalm of the Sons of Korah.

**2** Hear this, all peoples! Give ear, all inhabitants of the world,

**3** both low and high, rich and poor together!

**4** My mouth shall speak wisdom; the meditation of my heart shall be understanding.

**5** I will incline my ear to a proverb; I will solve my riddle to the music of the lyre.

**6** Why should I fear in times of trouble, when the iniquity of those who cheat me surrounds me,

**7** those who trust in their wealth and boast of the abundance of their riches?

**8** Truly no man can ransom another, or give to God the price of his life,

**9** for the ransom of their life is costly and can never suffice,

**10** that he should live on forever and never see the pit.

**11** For he sees that even the wise die; the fool and the stupid alike must perish and leave their wealth to others.

**12** Their graves are their homes forever, their dwelling places to all generations, though they called lands by their own names.

**13** Man in his pomp will not remain; he is like the beasts that perish.

**14** This is the path of those who have foolish confidence; yet after them people approve of their boasts. Selah.

**15** Like sheep they are appointed for Sheol; death shall be their shepherd, and the upright shall rule over them in the morning. Their form shall be consumed in Sheol, with no place to dwell.

**16** But God will ransom my soul from the power of Sheol, for He will receive me. Selah.

**17** Be not afraid when a man becomes rich, when the glory of his house increases.

**18** For when he dies he will carry nothing away; his glory will not go down after him.

**19** For though, while he lives, he counts himself blessed — and though they praise you when you do well for yourself —

**20** his soul will go to the generation of his fathers, who will never again see light.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 49.

- **49:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **49:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **49:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **49:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **49:13** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **49:17** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **49:16**: The verb 'takes me' (yiqqacheni) is the same used for Enoch (Gen 5:24) and Elijah (2 Kings 2:3). God 'takes' the righteous beyond death's reach.

### LOGOS
- **49:13**: The refrain: 'Man in his pomp will not remain; he is like the beasts that perish.' Wealth cannot distinguish humans from animals in the face of death.

### PNEUMA
- **49:8-9**: The most radical economic statement in the Psalms: no amount of money can buy immortality. Death is the great equalizer, and the market closes at the grave.

— SOPHIA
